column1: # Token families that denote one operation but that the two languages spell
# differently.  Column 1 is the canonical spelling both sides compare as; column 2 is
# the comma-separated family; column 3 records why the family is legitimate.
# A family does two things: every body check canonicalises it to column 1, and the
# family gets an occurrence check (the port must use it at least as often as the C body
# does).  The occurrence check is not optional: a note that merely allowed `memcpy` to
# be absent let a body with all three of doprnt's output copies deleted pass both

column3: std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping is the port's memcpy/mempcpy; gnulib's rpl_mempcpy keeps its C name
Rust spells C's va_arg macro as VaList::next_arg
gnulib's ckd_add stores the wrapped sum and reports overflow; Rust's overflowing_add is that pair (P-15)
same pair for ckd_mul
same pair for ckd_sub

C's `sizeof` is Rust's `size_of::<T> ()` (and `size_of_val` when only a place expression names the type, as in flexmember.h's `sizeof (((type *) 0)->member[0])`); the family's occurrence check then requires the port to spell it as often as the C body does
C's `alignof` is Rust's `align_of::<T> ()`, same rule

C's `local_if_set` bitfield (lisp.h 3080) is the mirror's `BLV_LOCAL_IF_SET` flag inside `u.s.bits` (lisp.rs 1971); the occurrence check is what makes `make_blv`'s clear (data.c 2170) and `set_internal`'s read (data.c 1766) survive a deletion, which the note-based exemption could not (review B's D1, P-78 residual 4)

lisp.h 313-314 keeps `insertion_type` as a 1-bit `bool_bf` field of `struct Lisp_Marker`, which the mirror packs into `bits` (lisp.rs 337-348); the reader is the mirror's `MARKER_INSERTION_TYPE_P` and the writer the same mask (`MARKER_INSERTION_TYPE`), so the family carries both spellings and its occurrence check keeps every read (undo.c) and every write (marker.c's copy-marker and set-marker-insertion-type) alive

itree.h 51-53 declares itree_node's three `bool_bf` bits (`red`, `rear_advance`, `front_advance`), which itree.rs packs into one `bits` byte with the ITREE_RED/ITREE_REAR_ADVANCE/ITREE_FRONT_ADVANCE masks (itree.rs 96-104, PORTING.md 1.3); the family's occurrence check keeps every read and every write of the bit alive

marker.c's two `CONSIDER` statement macros (C 100-136, C 277-315) cannot be `macro_rules!` in Rust (a macro cannot name the caller's locals), so each one's statement sequence lives in a helper function (see docs/ports/marker.md); the occurrence check keeps the port calling those helpers as often as C expands the macro (six times per conversion function)

window.h 462's 1-bit `suspend_auto_hscroll` field of `struct window` is packed into the mirror's `bits` word (window.rs 158's WINDOW_SUSPEND_AUTO_HSCROLL_SHIFT, PORTING.md 1.3); insdel.c 236 writes it (`w->suspend_auto_hscroll = 0`), and the family's occurrence check keeps that write alive

buffer.h's 1-bit `inhibit_shrinking` field of `struct buffer_text` is packed into the mirror's `bits` byte (buffer.rs 392's BUFFER_TEXT_INHIBIT_SHRINKING, PORTING.md 1.3); insdel.c 2053 reads it (`!current_buffer->text->inhibit_shrinking`), and the family's occurrence check keeps that read alive

buffer.h 716's 1-bit `long_line_optimizations_p` field of `struct buffer` is packed into the mirror's `bits` byte (buffer.rs 717/756's BUFFER_LONG_LINE_OPTIMIZATIONS_P, PORTING.md 1.3); composite.c reads it twice (C 1068, 1679) and the family's occurrence check keeps both reads alive

ccl.h 54's 1-bit `last_block` field of `struct ccl_program` is packed into the mirror's `bits` byte (ccl.rs's CCL_PROGRAM_LAST_BLOCK, PORTING.md 1.3); ccl.c reads it in CCL_READ_CHAR and writes it in `Fccl_execute_on_string`, and the family's occurrence check keeps both alive

ccl.h 57's 1-bit `quit_silently` field of `struct ccl_program` is packed into the mirror's `bits` byte (ccl.rs's CCL_PROGRAM_QUIT_SILENTLY, PORTING.md 1.3); `setup_ccl_program` writes it and `ccl_error_handler` reads it
